ideas.risks: The desired theorem may be false even in the two-expert case; standard adversarial examples may force dependence on the maximum delay rather than the comparator delay.
ideas.summary: Study the abstract component-wise delayed full-information experts problem with two arms: one fast arm with delay 0 and one slow arm with delay D. Prove or refute simultaneous regret bounds of order sqrt(T log N) to the fast arm and sqrt(T D log N) to the slow arm, with precise feedback timing.
ideas.title: Comparator-Specific Delay Test
ideas.why_promising: This is the exact missing lemma behind the adaptive truncation upper bound. A proof would yield a tail-adaptive market algorithm; a counterexample would prevent more wasted effort on max-delay masters.

ideas.risks: The monotonicity y_t(H,b) <= y_t(H',b) may not control adversarial late bonuses, and the useful algorithm may still pay the largest H.
ideas.summary: If the general heterogeneous-delay theorem fails, exploit the special nested structure of market truncations: for fixed quote b, r_t^H(b) is monotone in H. Try a decomposition into short-window base rewards plus delayed bonus increments, or a multiscale FTRL/Hedge analysis charging only the comparator window.
ideas.title: Nested-Window Adaptation
ideas.why_promising: The market surrogate rewards have more structure than arbitrary delayed experts. This could recover the oracle min_H {delta_T(H)+sqrt(T H)} bound without solving an impossible general problem.

ideas.risks: There may be an unavoidable information tradeoff, such as KL at least gamma^2/q, that makes the construction too weak for matching rates.
ideas.summary: Analyze a noisy common-parameter lower bound. Blocks share a hidden type, but terminal observations reveal it only partially. Compute the Bayes gap, KL/TV leakage, tail mass q, revenue separation gamma, and optimize over block length and number of blocks.
ideas.title: Noisy Common-Type Lower Bound
ideas.why_promising: It directly targets the failure mode of full-reveal repeated atoms while preserving one fixed comparator across blocks, which is the main unresolved route to matching power-tail lower rates.

ideas.risks: The abstract finite-grid construction may not be realizable by price paths, or persistent quotes may destroy the intended tail envelope.
ideas.summary: Use the finite-grid Psi_G characterization to design a multi-hypothesis codebook where theta selects one globally best quote among M quote levels, observations leak limited information, and Fano/Assouad gives a lower bound. Only after computing Psi_G, attempt to realize the reward curves as terminal price distributions.
ideas.title: Codebook Bayes-Gap Design
ideas.why_promising: It avoids the independent-bit collapse by keeping one global comparator, and the finite-grid value formula gives a precise diagnostic before doing delicate market realization.

ideas.risks: Separators may add common rewards that change comparator values, reveal too much, or worsen beta/delta tails.
ideas.summary: Investigate block-localization mechanisms for lower bounds under persistent quotes. Try monotone quote bands, common clearing spikes, or reset barriers, and calculate exactly whether old quotes can trade on later spikes and how this affects beta, Delta, delta, and the Bayes gap.
ideas.title: Persistent-Quote Localization
ideas.why_promising: Iteration 13 showed repeated atoms fail because old quotes remain live. A successful localization gadget would make multiblock lower bounds much more credible.

ideas.risks: This may only repackage delta_T(H) and still miss predictability/observability, so it may not produce a new characterization.
ideas.summary: Develop the last-exceedance identity from the solver attempt: for L_a=max{s<=T:P_s>a}, total fixed-quote reward is a(L_a-1)_+. Express truncation loss and value tails in terms of last-exceedance ages, then test whether a last-passage value-tail condition is cleaner than first-hitting beta.
ideas.title: Last-Exceedance Tail Calculus
ideas.why_promising: The comparator depends on last future exceedances, not raw first-hitting probabilities. This may sharpen upper bounds and explain exactly why raw beta is the wrong object.

ideas.risks: This is mostly theorem hygiene and will not solve scalar tails or matching rates; it depends on standard measurable-version facts being cited or proved cleanly.
ideas.summary: Finish the original-policy version of the payoff-measure dominated no-gap theorem: fix the common Borel seed/state policy model, invoke or prove standard randomization for stochastic kernels, prove completed-measurable-to-Borel implementation, and use one policy class consistently in finite-subclass and full-class values.
ideas.title: Original-Policy No-Gap Closure
ideas.why_promising: It would remove a major conditional caveat from the accepted infinite-class value characterization, making the theorem package substantially cleaner.

ideas.risks: A doubling or horizon-adaptive known-law policy may defeat the proposed obstruction; the result is a separate regime from the main horizon-aware minimax problem.
ideas.summary: Formalize the anytime known-law two-deadline obstruction using a deterministic super-growing sequence with pairs of deadlines at prices 1/2 and 1. Prove or refute that every horizon-free policy has linear regret on one deadline subsequence despite knowing the infinite sequence.
ideas.title: Anytime Known-Law Boundary
ideas.why_promising: It clarifies a quantifier boundary left open by the oracle lemma: known finite-horizon laws are trivial, but known infinite laws with unknown evaluation horizon may not be.
